prompt_en: A surreal photograph of a subject inhabiting impossible physical reality, where ordinary scale has visibly changed. In a quiet sunlit room, one woman holds open a tiny matchbox while an enormous old steam locomotive emerges from it. Use the supplied portrait as a visible appearance guide for her face, dark short bob and fine wispy bangs. Her softly parted lips and intent, affectionate concentration give this impossible discovery a warm intimate presence. She wears a faded cream linen dress. The huge black iron locomotive fills the lower two-thirds of the landscape frame, its round boiler front nearly as high as the woman's shoulders, its wheels resting on the parquet floor close to the camera. Its long body narrows impossibly as it curves upward and backward into the tiny open matchbox held beside her waist. The metal boiler, wheels and two rails remain one continuously visible three-dimensional construction across the abrupt change of scale. At the box's open end, a miniature section of railway is visibly inside the cardboard tray; the same two rails cross the thin cardboard lip and rapidly spread to full railway gauge just outside it. The engine's small rear section is visibly passing through that opening while its large front section already occupies the room. The cardboard lip lies clearly in front of the small metal section, with a narrow shadow at their crossing, so the boundary reads as physical passage. Black iron, small brass rivets and rails share the same surface detail across both scales. She stands behind and slightly left of the engine, with her face unobstructed above it. Her left palm supports the underside of the matchbox tray and her right thumb and fingers hold its sleeve aside, leaving the opening fully visible. Both elbows remain near her torso. At the opening, her supporting fingertips and the tiny rail section share the same depth plane, giving a direct local size comparison. Both feet are planted apart on clear parquet beside the rails. Her eyes follow the crossing at the matchbox lip. Pale wall, single window and ordinary wooden chair stay quiet around the immense engine, establishing room scale. Warm side light illuminates her face, hands and cardboard, then rakes the locomotive's iron and its grounded wheel shadows. Photograph at chest height from a front three-quarter angle, wide enough to include both hands, the full matchbox-to-engine connection, the boiler front, both feet and floor space. Believable photographic surface texture, fine analog grain, restrained warm color. The impossible continuous expansion from matchbox to room-sized train dominates the whole photograph.
